strings.WIN_Palm_Maple_Oak_desc:
Despite achieving nominal independence, the West Indies Federation still remains under the unfortunate grip of competing influences, in an unceasing tug of war of political favors and ravenous business initiatives.

While Canadian authorities still claw at any measure of control it can retain over their former colonies, ensuring they don't venture too far from the Commonwealth, the opposite side sees the US grasping at an opportunity to steer the archipelago towards its own direct sway.

And right in the middle, stuck between the hands pulling from each flank are the forgotten few that call the islands their home, with each pull peeling at the growing chafe felt by those slowly starting to realize that their newfound autonomy might only be in name.
strings.WIN_Caribbean_Shield_desc:
For the American defense doctrine, the Caribbean is, and always has been, its first bulwark against any threat of military insertion coming from the Atlantic.

Despite its days as a theater for submarine warfare during the Second World War being long gone, this strategic value hasn't changed; but the circumstances most certainly did.

If the newly founded Federation has as of yet complied in continuing to fulfill its territory's previous role as a critical maritime holdfast for the OFN, it's only a matter of time before the people living on the islands want to take the matter of its defense into their own hands.
strings.WIN_Shadow_Federation_desc:
In the heart of many of its inhabitants, the founding of the West Indies Federation is shared as a moment of pivotal triumph, the achievement of a two-decade-old dream of self-rule achieved from the yoke of the US and Canada.

But after the fireworks had faded and the chants grown silent, the new administration was faced with a challenging reality: they now held de jure authority over a series of islands upon which they held absolutely no real control.

In practice, things have barely changed, and in most cases, day-to-day rule is still exercised by the same local councils as before, while the federation's central government struggles under the weight of its own political squabbles.
strings.WIN_Lost_at_Sea_desc:
The lack of genuine authority exercised by the Federation's central government means that in practice, each local administration is left to its own devices, especially in matters pertaining to economic planning.

Without any kind of unified direction, the archipelago has turned into a maze of conflicting policies, with one islet following its own carefully monitored development scheme while its neighbour thrives as a hotbed of free market laissez-faire.

Beyond being an administrative headache to keep track of, this disharmonious development proves to be a serious hindrance to any kind of organized trade between the islands, or even in issues as benign as establishing a coherent customs or immigration doctrine.
strings.WIN_Pan_Caribbean_Dream_desc:
For the first time in history, the people of the West Indies have been united as one, in a country that they may call their own. A fact that will remain true even in the face of all the severe issues troubling the newborn Federation.

Its myriad member states might linger on the same inter-island rivalries as prior, and its government be no more than a shell facing backlash at any real measure of control it may try to assert over the local councils.

Yet despite these constant quarrels, each of the competing voices urging their own path for the archipelago's future does so in enthusiasm toward a dream shared by all: that of a truly Caribbean nation, both in name and spirit.
strings.WIN_Enter_Hurricane_desc:
Stalwartly emerging through the strife surrounding its establishment, the newborn West Indies Federation would enter the next decade with its eyes shining with promises of a bright and prosperous future for its denizens.

Only for the Oil Crisis to wipe all of these hopes away.

Now, what remains of these idealistic foundations is an administration struggling to pull the myriad of islands under its authority away from impending economic collapse. Unless it finds the means to reform its crumbling institutions or the salvatory hand of an outside benefactor, it seems the central government will be powerless to stop these dreams of independence from ending in tragic disaster.
strings.WIN_Maple_Autumn_desc:
After the dust settled and the white papers and communiqués slowed down enough to be legible, it became clear that the status quo of the West Indies Federation was to be continued under closer Canadian supervision. With this decision being finalised, the Dominion of Canada seems ascendant in their patronage and influence over the federation. The liberal chauvinistic vision all parties in the Canadian Parliament have held in respect to the governance and future of the WIF appears unshakeable.

Though the average foreign-policy enthusiast in Canada may be joyful at the continuance of Canada “fulfilling its duty to uplift and enlighten” the peoples of the WIF, said peoples are nowhere near as enthusiastic. Large swathes of the citizenry chafe at the seeming neocolonialism of the new system. A greater problem that large swathes of Parliament seem ignorant of at the moment is American skepticism. Looking on from Langley, Foggy Bottom, and elsewhere in the Potomac River valley, Uncle Sam makes no secret of his doubt that Canada will be able to hack it a second time.
strings.WIN_Follow_North_Star_desc:
Amidst the chaos of the Oil Crisis and accompanying economic collapse, the Canadian government has taken action to stabilise the situation in the West Indies. Assuming control for general economic planning, the Canadians have sold off distressed state assets to Canadian and American corporations and enforcing a diminishing number of state-sanctioned monopolies.

Many citizens of the West Indies regard the Canadian measures as neo-imperialistic in nature, more focused with the Canadian Department of Finance's bottom line than the welfare of those Canada purports to “help”. Others, observing that Canada has also propped up the preexisting social-safety nets with loans and oversight, consider Canadian economic command and control to be preferable to complete economic collapse.
strings.WIN_Sturdy_Oak_desc: The maple tree of Canadian dominance in the West Indian Federation has fallen over, reduced to a blasted stump under the strain of the Oil Crisis. A sturdy oak—American rule—has had to be propped up in its place. America takes up this task with little enthusiasm; not desirous of wasting time or resources on the region's political development, Washington had been content to leave it to Canada... until things went to hell on Canada's watch. Ottawa is unfit for purpose. The peoples of the Caribbean are hardly any better off, riven by division and tortured by economic uncertainty. No matter how much America might kick and scream, it falls to Uncle Sam to make the concept of the “American lake” a reality.
strings.WIN_New_Captain_desc:
The West Indies Federation has not had much choice in the decisions it takes. Before, it was Ottawa that would dictate terms to it; today, Washington has taken that role. These days are no exception: in exchange for an American-led bailout, the WIF has been “invited” to accept a plan of massive economic overhaul pioneered by the rising economic star Thomas Sowell.

Sowell, a Chicago-educated economist, intends to turn the West Indies into a showpiece for his radical economic liberalism. To that end he focuses obsessively on breaking down protectionist measures and other such trade barriers, slashing taxes and “red tape”, and busting the “collectivist” unions that he perceives as making investment difficult. Whether the West Indies like it or not, a new, more capitalist era has dawned in these islands.
strings.WIN_United_States_Caribbean_desc:
Further to other economic and political changes brought about by the replacement of exile-influenced Canadian paternalism with Chicago-influenced American paternalism, the West Indies Federation has also undergone a total rework of its governing apparatus. The new WIF is more strictly a federation; increased power has been centralised upon the capital, while at the same time more governance is devolved upon the various islands.

The American federalist model has sufficed for American purposes, but part of that is brought about by the connectedness and relative homogeneity of the United States compared to the Caribbean. The WIF is composed entirely of discontiguous islands, and has more ethnic groups in a single island than America often hosts in several states; accordingly, whether this new governance will actually be a good fit for the West Indies remains to be seen.
strings.WIN_Young_Palm_desc:
Narrowly avoiding certain economic demise with the help of a providential bail-out, the precarious archipelago now finds itself left to carve its own way out of the recent crisis, with both Canadian and American authorities choosing to take a more hands-off approach despite the lingering instability.

However, this comes at the irritation of both those who would have hoped for the opportunity of some long-overdue reform to the Federation's quivering structure, and those who consider yet another influx of money from the west as further proof that the looming shadow of their colonial overlords is never quite far.
strings.WIN_Federate_or_Die_desc:
With the approval of the reform plans jointly proposed by Eric Williams and the Federal Labour Party, the Federation now undergoes a process of rapid centralisation, aiming to leave the government in Bridgetown more adequately equipped to administer the archipelago's many individual member states.

This, of course, comes at the chafe of those who cherished the relative autonomy that their own islands had until now enjoyed, leading to growing concerns as the balance shifts between proponents of increased state control and those advocating for preserving the decentralised status quo.
strings.WIN_Charting_Course_desc:
For the first time, the West Indies Federation can make a claim of being master in its own house. It intends to take this newfound freedom with both hands. Armed with newfound powers and increased revenue generation, the newly-centralising West Indies Federation plans for a bold new era of economic development radiating out from its capital of Bridgetown.

Inspired by Trinidadian state-driven developmentalist plans and backed by Trinidad's oil money, the WIF has begun the hard work of moving away from the plantation economy of old and turning the West Indies into a modern nation providing social services to all its citizens. The journey will be protracted by funding questions and the resistance of entrenched economic interests, but the West Indies Federation seems set on staying this course no matter the cost.
